mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to tightened near-term discounting of corporate cash flows.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative whenever the trigger occurs, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS spikes and negative 20d returns is statistically insignificant (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in UNRATE above 4.5% signals labor market weakness, which reduces consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In regimes where UNRATE > 4.5%, the 60-day forward returns are non-negative more than 60% of the time, or the predictive power of UNRATE changes on SPX 60d returns is below 0.05 (AICc).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDP demand proxy GDPC1 exceeds 2% above its 12-month moving average, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days are positive as market anticipates stronger economic momentum.
failure_condition: Across 20 test windows where the trigger occurs, 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (two-tailed t-test, p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below its 12-month average indicates softening supply conditions, which raises the risk of overcapacity and suppresses equity valuations, producing negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In 30 instances of INDPRO < INDPRO[12m], the 20-day forward returns are non-negative more than 50% of the time, or the IC is above 0.05 over a 6-month window.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of RSAFS above 700 billion suggests persistent excess demand, which, if sustained, elevates equity risk premia and yields negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The interaction of RSAFS > 700 for two consecutive months with SPX 20d returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly PAYEMS exceeds 160,000 by more than 10% relative to the prior month, it indicates a sudden surge in job creation that temporarily boosts investor sentiment and produces positive 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In regimes where PAYEMS spikes occur, 60-day forward returns remain negative more than 70% of the time, or the IC is below -0.1 over a 3-month window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in CPIAUCSL (monthly inflation) below 3% triggers a risk-off reaction as markets anticipate lower future rate cuts, producing negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: During 10 such CPIAUCSL < 3.0 events, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (industrial production) falls by more than 2% in a month versus the prior month, it signals supply disruptions that persistently depress earnings growth and drive negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Across 8 such monthly drops, the 60-day forward returns are non-negative more than 50% of the time, or the predictive power of HOUST changes on SPX 60d returns is below 0.04 (AICc).
